answer: Local cluster licensing. An agent may transact only if its address shares a recent routing neighborhood with its counterparty: each node forwards a signed receipt for every peer it successfully relays to, keeping a small island of mutually observed links. Sybil clusters fail because fabricated receipts don’t match the live relay graph. Each fake identity must sustain real forwarding traffic and latency to keep its kernel of receipts fresh, costing bandwidth and uptime per identity; stale relics drop from routing tables.
